flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring from regularity that the two possible endpoint orbits of an edge must coincide. Edge-transitivity shows only that there are at most two vertex orbits; if there are two, every edge joins the two orbits. Equal degrees imply equal orbit sizes, but do not imply that an automorphism swaps the orbits.
counterexample: The Gray graph is a finite simple cubic edge-transitive graph that is not vertex-transitive.
assessment_summary: Step 1 is justified: fix an edge {u,v}; every vertex lies on an edge and edge-transitivity maps that edge to {u,v}, so every vertex belongs to the orbit of u or v. The attempted proof then fails at Step 2. Regular bipartite edge-transitive graphs can retain two distinct vertex orbits (semisymmetric graphs), so the statement is false.
